tournaments.note: Won by Poland, 2–1 over Switzerland in the final.

tournaments.name: Davis Cup Qualifiers, first round
tournaments.note: 13 ties between national teams; the winners advanced to the second round.

tournaments.name: Davis Cup Qualifiers, second round
tournaments.note: The 7 winners qualified for the Final 8 in Bologna.

tournaments.name: Rolex Paris Masters
tournaments.note: Paris La Defense Arena. Qualifying on 31 October and 1 November, main draw from 2 November. Qualifiers: Tomas Machac, Benjamin Bonzi, Mattia Bellucci, Alex Molcan, Juan Manuel Cerundolo, Lorenzo Sonego, Rinky Hijikata. Alexander Blockx withdrew with an ankle injury on 2 November; lucky loser Sebastian Baez replaced him.

tournaments.name: Nitto ATP Finals
tournaments.note: Inalpi Arena. The top eight in the Race to Turin, two groups of four. Qualified so far: Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Ben Shelton. Jannik Sinner qualified but ended his season with a knee injury. The group draw takes place after Stockholm.

tournaments.name: Next Gen ATP Finals
tournaments.note: Season finale for the best players aged 20 and under.

tournaments.name: United Cup
tournaments.note: Mixed team event. Won by Poland, 2–1 over Switzerland in the final.

tournaments.name: Billie Jean King Cup Finals
tournaments.note: Won by Czechia (12th title), 2–0 over Ukraine in the final. Czech captain: Barbora Strycova.

tournaments.name: Chennai Open
tournaments.note: Qualifying on 31 October and 1 November. Qualifiers: Aliona Falei, Kyoka Okamura, Zhibek Kulambayeva, Weronika Falkowska. Guangzhou finalists Lilli Tagger and Harriet Dart withdrew; lucky losers Mei Yamaguchi and Viktorija Morvayova entered. The opening day on 2 November was washed out by rain from Cyclonic Storm Murasu; first-round matches move to 3 November.

tournaments.name: Hong Kong Tennis Open
tournaments.note: Qualifying on 31 October and 1 November. Kaitlin Quevedo and Xinran Sun withdrew after reaching the Guangzhou semifinals.

tournaments.name: Jiangxi Open
tournaments.note: Not on the November 2026 calendar: the Jiangxi Open was held on 4–10 May 2026 as a WTA 125 event.

tournaments.name: WTA Finals
tournaments.note: Indian Wells Tennis Garden. The top eight in the Race, two groups of four. Qualified: Elena Rybakina, Aryna Sabalenka, Mirra Andreeva, Jessica Pegula, Coco Gauff, Elina Svitolina, Karolina Muchova, Linda Noskova. The group draw has not taken place yet.

basel.note: Line order in the draw is reconstructed from results; the pairings are exact. Seeds: 2 Fils, 6 Fritz, 8 Lehecka.

davis-finals.note: Each tie is two singles and one doubles. Start times have not been announced yet.

laver-cup.note: Team Europe (captain Yannick Noah) won 13–5. Matches 11 and 12 were not played because Europe had reached 13 points. Square brackets mark a deciding match tiebreak to 10.

paris.note: 56-player draw; the top eight seeds start in the second round. Main draw from 2 November, final on 8 November. Qualifying on 31 October and 1 November; the last seven qualifying matches were the final round on 1 November. Alexander Blockx withdrew on 2 November with an ankle injury; lucky loser Sebastian Baez took his place against Daniel Merida. On 3 November play starts at 11:00 local time with the remaining first-round matches; Andrey Rublev vs Tomas Martin Etcheverry, Arthur Rinderknech vs Francisco Cerundolo and Quentin Halys vs Arthur Fery open the day, Alex Michelsen vs Jiri Lehecka is not before 15:00 and Benjamin Bonzi vs Taylor Fritz not before 15:30. Ben Shelton also plays his opening match on 3 November.

vienna.note: Line order in the draw is reconstructed from results; the pairings are exact.

wta-bjk-finals.note: Final: Karolina Muchova d. Anhelina Kalinina 6–2, 6–3; Linda Noskova d. Elina Svitolina 6–3, 7–6(5). Shenzhen Bay Sports Centre Arena.

wta-chennai.note: Main draw from 2 November, final on 8 November. The opening day on 2 November was washed out by rain from Cyclonic Storm Murasu, so all 16 first-round matches move to 3 November, with play from about 11:00 local time. Lilli Tagger and Harriet Dart withdrew after reaching the Guangzhou final. Lucrezia Stefanini moved into Tagger's place in the draw and lucky loser Mei Yamaguchi took Stefanini's original spot; lucky loser Viktorija Morvayova replaced Dart.

wta-guangzhou.note: Line order in the draw is reconstructed from results; the pairings are exact.

wta-hong-kong.note: Main draw from 2 November, final on 8 November. Opening day on 2 November starts at 14:00 local time with Viktorija Golubic vs Katie Boulter; Venus Williams opens the evening session on Centre Court. Qualifying: the first eight matches are round one (31 October), the last four are the final round (1 November). Qualifiers: Aliaksandra Sasnovich, Himeno Sakatsume, Tatiana Prozorova, Alexandra Shubladze. Kaitlin Quevedo and Xinran Sun withdrew; lucky losers Elena Pridankina and Carol Young Suh Lee took their places. Leylah Fernandez vs Sofia Kenin and Antonia Ruzic vs Alina Charaeva were moved from 2 to 3 November. On 3 November play starts at 14:00 local time on all courts; the Centre Court evening session starts not before 18:30.

wta-tokyo.note: Line order in the draw is reconstructed from results; the pairings are exact. Rybakina withdrew before the quarterfinal. Final on Sunday 1 November at 12:00 Tokyo time.
